name: Alma Provider Platform
one_liner: $125/mo platform with AI notes, EHR, and weekly pay. Hit by 2024 Optum cuts (up to 30%) and 2026 Aetna cuts. Acquired by Spring Health.
short_description: Alma is a membership-based platform for independent therapists bundling insurance credentialing, billing, AI session notes, EHR, scheduling, and a client-facing directory.
long_description: Alma is an all-in-one platform for independent mental health providers that combines insurance credentialing, in-network billing, AI-powered session notes (Note Assist), EHR, scheduling, and a therapist directory—all for $125/month ($95/month billed annually). Alma helps therapists get credentialed with major insurers like Aetna, Cigna, UnitedHealthcare, Oscar, and Oxford, often negotiating $10-30 higher per-session reimbursement rates than solo credentialing. The platform handles all insurance billing and pays therapists weekly (vs. Headway's bi-weekly). In January 2026, Spring Health acquired Alma, creating one of the largest mental health platforms in the US. Alma also provides robust peer consultation groups, continuing education, and access to clinical advisors including Esther Perel, Lori Gottlieb, and Guy Winch. The $500 provider referral bonus incentivizes network growth.
best_for: Independent therapists wanting premium reimbursement rates
Providers seeking an all-in-one platform (credentialing + EHR + AI notes)
Clinicians valuing community features (peer consultation, CE)
Therapists who can see 20+ sessions/week (ROI on membership)
not_for: Clinicians with very low session volume
Those only needing credentialing without EHR

faqs.q: How much does Alma cost for therapists?
faqs.a: Alma costs $125/month or $95/month with annual billing ($1,140/year). There is no free trial or free tier, unlike competitors like Headway.

faqs.q: Is Alma worth the cost vs Headway?
faqs.a: Alma often negotiates $10-30 higher reimbursement rates per session than solo credentialing. At 20 sessions/week, even a $10 increase generates $800/month extra revenue—more than covering the membership. Alma also includes AI notes, EHR, and weekly payments (vs. Headway bi-weekly).

faqs.q: What is Alma's relationship with Spring Health?
faqs.a: Spring Health acquired Alma in January 2026, creating one of the largest mental health platforms in the US. Alma continues to operate under its own brand.

Alma includes insurance credentialing, in-network billing, AI-powered Note Assist for session notes, EHR with assessments and treatment plans, scheduling, client matching through a provider directory, peer consultation groups, and continuing education.
